h1: Lock formers and HVAC duct machines — Pittsburgh lock formers, roll formers and duct tools
intro: A lock former (Pittsburgh machine) rolls the edge of a duct panel into the Pittsburgh lock — the pocket the matching flange is hammered into to close a rectangular duct — and, with other roll sets, double seams, drive cleats, button locks and flanges. NovoTech's value-line HVAC machines are built in China to our specification: the PF20G lock former for 26 – 20 ga, the PF16G for 25 – 16 ga with six roll forms as standard, and the AX20G auxiliary roll former whose roll sets change in under five minutes; and the tools that finish the duct — the SL-10 electric seam closer, hand brakes and cleat benders, round duct rollers, a power beading machine for round duct and a slitting and bending machine. Parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What is a Pittsburgh lock, and what gauge can a lock former take?
faq.a: The Pittsburgh lock is the standard longitudinal seam of rectangular duct: the lock former rolls a pocket on one edge of the panel, the other edge is bent to a 90° flange, the flange goes into the pocket and the lip is hammered (or closed with a seam closer) over it. The PF20G forms it in 26 to 20 ga, the PF16G in 25 to 16 ga mild steel; galvanized steel is the usual material.

The PF20G is the compact lock former for light duct — Pittsburgh, flange attachment and right angle in 26 – 20 ga, with double seam and drive cleat rolls as options. The PF16G takes duct to 16 ga and has six roll forms as standard — Pittsburgh, flange attachment, right angle, double seam, drive cleat and Z — on one machine. The AX20G is an auxiliary roll former for the joints a lock former does not make: button locks, Acme double seams, drive cleats and a 6-in-1 set of flanges and standing seams, with roll sets that change in five minutes.

faq.q: How much material does a Pittsburgh lock use?
faq.a: About 1″ of sheet for the pocket; the adjustable auto-guides set the edge so the pocket depth is consistent and material waste stays at a minimum. Allow for it when you lay out the blanks.

faq.q: Do I need a seam closer?
faq.a: For a few ducts a week the lip is closed with a hammer. For production the SL-10 runs along the seam and closes it in three stages — 30°, 75°, 90° — adjusting itself to the sheet thickness: faster, quieter and a neater seam than hammering.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
